title: The Great God Pan — What Science Actually Says #Shorts
description:
Meaning is not found in The Great God Pan — it is manufactured for it. The Great God Pan is an 1894 horror and fantasy novella by the Welsh writer Arthur Machen. Machen was inspired to write The Great God Pan by his experiences at the ruins of a pagan temple in Wales.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — The Great God Pan shows exactly where that breaks. Reviewing the novella for the magazine Literary News, Richard Henry Stoddard criticised the story as "too morbid to be the production of a healthy mind". The art critic Harry Quilter's review of the book, titled "The Gospel of Intensity", and published in The Contemporary Review in June 1895, was even more harsh.
